Instrument (EN): Binge Eating Disorder Screener-7 — Chilean Spanish psychometric adaptation
Question count: 7 (full screener); factor CFA on 4 symptom items only
Scales / measured domains (EN): Loss of control (2 fitted symptom indicators); Eating-related emotional distress (2 fitted indicators). Three screening/gating items excluded from factor analysis, not absent from full BEDS-7.
Research provenance: Escandón-Nagel N et al., Journal of Eating Disorders 14:138, published 2026-05-02; DOI 10.1186/s40337-026-01623-9; Spanish translated/backtranslated original 7 items; Chilean adult elevated-symptom sample N435 of 1497 interested; 2-factor CFA based on items 3-6; global omega .706. Highly selected participants, 94.5% screened positive; no independent diagnostic sensitivity/specificity established for Chilean version.
DB locales: No published BEDS/ES version in Supabase app.assessment_versions, read only 2026-10-24 (145 keys/230 EN150 RU80 ES0).
EN form: Original US English 7-item screener from Shire/Takeda-related authors (Herman et al 2016), not new EN validation here.
RU form: No RU respondent validation found in this Chilean paper.
ES form: ES-CL respondent items translated/back-translated and studied N435; three gating items had near-zero variance and were not in CFA; not equivalent to nationwide ES norms.
Other translations: No other-language forms established by this paper.
Target population: Chilean adults with overweight/obesity, >=2 binge episodes last month, enriched sample N435 (BMI groups and activity, not general population).
Commercial digital use / permission revi: BEDS-7 originated from Shire Development; Takeda Canada 2021 BEDS7 form asserts all rights reserved. CC BY article does not license screener item copying, adapted translation, algorithm, public digital administration or commercial platform. Seek owner + Chilean translator written authorization and clinical governance.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / LICENSED_ONLY. Screening not diagnosis; model uses 4 variable items, original 7-question gate algorithm not cross-validated for ES-CL. Limited representativeness, eating-disorder safeguarding, no prompts, scoring, thresholds or deployment.

Instrument (EN): Binge Eating Disorder Screener-9 — exploratory Chilean Spanish BEDS-7 extension
Scales / measured domains (EN): Exploratory two-factor model: loss of control and emotional distress with additional binge-eating behaviors; final factor fit included 6 variable items and excluded 3 gating/low-variation items.
Research provenance: Same Escandón-Nagel et al. 2026 Chilean sample N435 and DOI 10.1186/s40337-026-01623-9 as BEDS-7, NOT an independent validation. BEDS-9 added two DSM-5-based items after experts; two-factor CFA/ESEM had acceptable fit, but global omega only .544 (95%CI .358-.729), so rejected in favor of BEDS-7; NO validated BEDS-9 scale or cutoffs.
DB locales: No published BEDS-9 definition/version in Supabase 2026-10-24; unique edition only, shared publication/sample with BEDS-7.
EN form: Original English BEDS-7 is separate; no independent EN BEDS-9 validation established.
ES form: ES-CL: exploratory N435 respondent variant created by adding two items to Spanish BEDS7; studied but NOT recommended or validated due to omega .544.
Target population: Same nonrepresentative Chilean N435 high-symptom adults as BEDS-7 paper, not a second cohort.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Third-party BEDS-7 base (Shire/Takeda) copyrighted, modified instrument compounds translation and derivative rights. Article CC BY is not a commercial derivative questionnaire grant. Seek explicit permissions before any publication.
Validated edition evidence / links: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13281422/ ; factor fit and reliability Results/Table 5-6; CC BY article with third-party carveout.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / EXPLORATORY / NOT VALIDATED. Low reliability and no cross-validated prediction. Count as research edition only, NOT new independently validated ES form; do not score, deploy, or promote.

Instrument (EN): Loyola Generativity Scale — Chilean Spanish 14-item teacher-specific three-factor model
Question count: 14 fitted final factor items (20 administered; 4 filtered to 16; further 2 absent from final model table)
Scales / measured domains (EN): Generative Inefficacy (3); Generative Action (8); Generative Legacy (3). Neither original 20-item two-domain scores nor broad adult norms can be substituted.
Research provenance: Sandoval-Obando et al., Frontiers in Psychology 17:1913448, 2026-08-26, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1913448; N430 Chilean primary teachers (two 215-person internally split samples, not independent validations). Spanish translated/adapted from English LGS 20; four items failed MSA, 16 retained for analysis, final Table 5 contains 14 item loadings; 3-factor CFA; inconsistent description of 16-vs-14 final items requires author confirmation.
DB locales: No published LGS key or exact Chilean teacher model in active Supabase as of 2026-10-24.
EN form: Original LGS-20 created in English by McAdams & de St. Aubin 1992; this study does not newly validate English 14-item form.
RU form: No RU respondent form validated here.
ES form: ES-CL respondent translation tested on N430 Chilean primary educators; 14 final factor indicators (Table 5), but author confirmation of final reproducible item list and score definition needed.
Target population: 430 voluntary Chilean primary teachers across four regions (76% women); two internally split halves n215; not general adult, therapeutic or worker norms.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Frontiers paper CC BY does not grant original McAdams scale commercial item/derivative redistribution rights. Seek written original developer and Chilean translation authorization for commercial online administration and verify original/shortened scoring.
